A poem, a poem. The words of the poem are in the first person singular, though they could as easily be plural. A poem written as if you were there at the time. As if it were really happening. As if you were a part of it.

I am standing at the entrance to the chamber, with the door open behind me and the long passage before me. It’s not a very long way – just a few hundred feet perhaps – but it feels like I am walking into infinity.

The floor is smooth and white, polished. My steps echo, resounding, sounding like the footsteps of giants.

.

i found a small hole in your soul.
I tried to mend it with my broken sythe
but I couldn’t, it was too much, too big,
and I was too little to reach.

So i went away, and i flew around the world.
I visited all the corners of the universe
and collected all the pieces of my soul,
all the shards and scraps and broken edges,
all the parts of me that had fallen out
and been swept away into the sky.

I found all of them,
and I put them back together,
and then I flew towards you again,
and now i can fix your soul.
I am whole, I am complete.
I have gathered up the pieces of me
that were lost.
I am one again.

so come with me.
we’ll fly to the edge of the sky.
We’ll sit on the moon.
I’ll make your soul whole again,
and I’ll put my pieces into yours,
and we will be two again.
And our souls will be one.
